class electrip.control_ui.Animator(method, start_val, end_val, step, duration)[source]¶

Bases: gi._gobject._gobject.GObject, threading.Thread

Calls method at a regular interval, linearly increasing the parameter from start_val to end_val. duration specifies the duration of the animation, step specifies the resolution of the animation as the amount of increase per interval. When end_val is reached, the signal ‘animation-finished’ is emitted.

class electrip.control_ui.ControllerHub(socket_thread, emergency_button, h_adjustment)[source]¶

Bases: gi.repository.Gtk.Grid

Gtk.Grid which fills itself with LocoController- instances. Responsible for creating a EventHandlerThread and taking over gamepad-event-handling via EventHandlerThread.gamepad_init() if pygame is available.

change_loco(loco_id, new_loco_id, gamepad)[source]¶

Makes gamepad switch from controlling the Loco with loco_id to the Loco with new_loco_id. If auto-focus is active, makes the corresponding controller focus itself in the window. Attention: This is an internal method. No error handling is done here. Use scroll() instead.

check_acceleration()[source]¶

Iterates over all initialized Gamepad-objects and sets the acceleration of the corresponding Loco according to the deviation of the acceleration-axis of the gamepad.

gamepad_button_pressed(gamepad, button)[source]¶

Checks if the pressed button is assigned an action at the LocoController belonging to gamepad (e.g. switching a loco-function) or if it is assigned a global action (e.g. reverse loco direction, emergency stop ...)

gamepad_button_released(gamepad, button)[source]¶

Checks if the toggle-mode of a function in a LocoController identified by gamepad and button is of kind “PUSH” or “PUSH_LIMITED” (comp. config.loco_functions.ToggleMode). If such function exists its state is switched.

horiz_joyhat_moved(gamepad, direction)[source]¶

Makes gamepad scroll to the next loco in direction.

quit()[source]¶
scroll(direction, gamepad)[source]¶

Assigns the gamepad another loco to control, namely either the one at the controller at the right (direction == True) or the left side (direction == False) of the currently assigned loco.

set_auto_scroll(direction, gamepad)[source]¶

This method is called 500 ms after the joyhat has been pushed in direction (-1 or 1). If the joyhat is still pushed in the same direction, auto-scrolling in direction is activated, meaning scroll() will be called every 60 ms until the joyhat is released.

concurrent Module¶

class electrip.concurrent.SocketThread(socket, timeout=2)[source]¶

Bases: threading.Thread

Thread implementing strictly sequential socket- communication from a client-perspective: It sends commands and the other side (the server) has to reply with information about its new state or errors. Provides non-blocking methods to add commands to the internal queue, the reply will be printed as soon as it was received using locked_print(). Prints error messages if more than 20 unanswered commands are pending in the queue or timeout is reached.

quit()[source]¶
run()[source]¶
send_and_wait_for_answer(cmd)[source]¶

Non-blocking method which adds cmd to the queue of commands to be sent to the server.

wait_for_answer()[source]¶

Blocks for a server-reply until the timeout is reached.

electrip.concurrent.locked_print(*args)[source]¶

Acquires print_lock and then prints like the normal print-statement. Calling this method consequently ensures nice output when multiple threads are printing.

pygame_io Module¶

class electrip.pygame_io.DieselSoundController(handler_thread, loco_engine, volume)[source]¶

Bases: electrip.pygame_io.SoundController

A SoundController for DieselEngine-instances. Have a look at DieselEngine and DieselSoundSegment to understand how it works.

The DieselSoundController emits three signals which can be used to synchronize the UI:

  • sound-level-changed: emitted when a new sound segment is reached and the transition begins
  • engine-idle: emitted when the diesel-engine runs idle and the loco is standing still (after the loco has been driving)
  • engine-stopped: emitted when the shutdown-process of the engine has completed

class electrip.pygame_io.EventHandlerThread(sampling_rate)[source]¶

Bases: threading.Thread

Class for pygame event handling. Deals with joystick input and sound output.

acquire_channel_id()[source]¶

Registers a new audio-channel, returning its id for usage with other methods of EventHandlerThread. A maximum of 254 channels may be acquired (if exceeded an exception will be raised).

add_callback(channel_id, callback_func, *args)[source]¶

Adds callback_func to the list of functions which should be called when the channel with channel_id finished playing a sound. This is needed to implement gapless-playback of a stream of sounds, because pygame allows only one sound at a time to be queued for gapless playback on a channel. E.g.:

# create a Sound-object to be played:
tchoo = pygame.mixer.Sound("tchoo.ogg")

# define a callback-function:
def repeat_sound():
    handler_thread.queue(tchoo)

# assuming handler_thread is an EventHandlerThread-instance:
channel_id = handler_thread.acquire_channel_id()
handler_thread.add_callback(channel_id, repeat_sound)
handler_thread.double_queue_sound(tchoo)

# 'repeat_sound' will now be called whenever a sound on
# channel with channel_id finishes, allowing to put the next
# sound in the queue for gapless playback
add_quit_callback(callback_func)[source]¶

Adds callback_func to the list of functions which should be called when quit() is called.

double_queue_sound(channel_id, sound)[source]¶

Calls pygame.mixer.Channel.queue() on the channel with channel_id twice. Results in the channel playing sound and having sound in the queue, which is useful to start gapless playback. sound is allowed to be None, nothing will happen then.

gamepad_init(button_pressed_cb, button_released_cb, horiz_joyhat_moved_cb, max_gamepads=-1)[source]¶

This method must be called before EventHandlerThread.start() is called, as it prepares the EventHandlerThread for gamepad-usage. The ..._cb-arguments specify callback-methods for the following events:

  • button_pressed_cb(gmp, button): button at gamepad gmp was pressed
  • button_released_cb(gmp, button): button at gamepad gmp was released
  • joyhat_moved_horiz_cb(gmp, direction): joyhat at gamepad gmp was moved to the left (direction == -1), the right (direction == 1) or released (direction == 0).

max_gamepads specifies the highest allowed number of Gamepad-objects to be created by the EventHandlerThread.

Returns the number of gamepads which are in use after initialization.

queue_sound(channel_id, sound)[source]¶

class electrip.pygame_io.SoundController(handler_thread, loco_engine, volume)[source]¶

Bases: gi._gobject._gobject.GObject

Abstract base class for sound controllers using a Engine-object loco_engine and the EventHandlerThread-instance handler_thread for sound-playback. volume specifies the volume of the engine as a float from 0 to 1. The work done by a SoundController consists of two parts:

    1. Playback of the EventSound-objects from loco_engine.event_sounds. This happens automatically.
    1. Playback of engine-sounds, according to the current speed of the loco. This part must be dealt with in the child class.

How (2) works: Generally, the SoundController leaves most of the actual implementation to the child classes, to ensure high flexibility.

Still, child classes must

  • use self.mixer (the reference to handler_thread) to control playback according to the current speed of the loco.
  • implement the get_engine_is_running-method
  • implement the do...-methods

E.g. an implementation to start a Diesel-engine in a subclass could be:

class DieselSoundController(SoundController):
    # ...
    
    def do_start_engine(self):
        # queue the startup-sound and the idle-sound
        self.mixer.queue_sound(some_channel_id, self.engine.start_sound)
        self.mixer.queue_sound(some_channel_id, self.engine.idle_sound)

Plays shutdown sound if the engine is not moving and makes sure there is no sound emission afterwards.

Calls do_start_engine_at_speed() if the engine is not running, otherwise does nothing.

class electrip.widgets.ControlPointGraph(x_legend_text, y_legend_text, x_res_list, y_res_list)[source]¶

Bases: gi.repository.Gtk.DrawingArea

Graph-widget allowing to edit a LinearSegmentFunction visually in a cartesian coordinate system. x_legend_text and y_legend_text specify the labels for the x- and y-axis as tuples of the form (x_var_name, x_full_name) where x/y_var_name is the variable name (e.g. 't') and x/y_full_name is the longer description (e.g. 'time in secs'). x_res_list and y_res_list are lists containing acceptable resolutions for the x- and y-axis.

Behaviour:

  • Left-click: Creates a new control-point
  • Left-click on an existing point + drag: Moves the control-point with the mouse
  • Right-click on an existing point: Removes the control-point

class electrip.widgets.EntryTable(use_tooltips, use_bold_labels, orientation=<enum GTK_ORIENTATION_VERTICAL of type GtkOrientation>, end=None)[source]¶

Bases: gi.repository.Gtk.Grid

Provides a UI to set attributes on configuration objects. Allows you to stop caring about signal-handling and layout.

If use_tooltips is True, the descriptions are provided as tooltips. Otherwise the description will appear behind the ui-elements. If use_bold_labels is True, the labels for the object-attributes appear in bold font.

New input-elements can be added using the ‘add_(some_element)’-methods, where the first two arguments specify the label and the description-text for the respective attribute.

Have a look at the following example:

# NOTE: we assume a Loco-instance called 'loco'
# has already been created

# choose layout-options on creation
table = EntryTable(True, False)

# add a combo-box which operates on loco.protocol
table.add_combo_entry("Protokoll",
                      "Das Digitalprotokoll, welches"
                      "vom Decoder verwendet wird.",
                      "protocol",
                      GObject.TYPE_STRING,
                      (("M 1", "Märklin Motorola Version 1"),
                       ("M 2", "Märklin Motorola Version 2"),
                       ("N 1", "DCC kurzes Adressformat"),
                       ("N 2", "DCC langes Adressformat")))

# you can add more ui-elements for different attributes 
table.add_...

# load the protocol value from loco
# and the others you have specified
table.load(loco)

# now, if the user selects "Märklin Motorola Version 1",
# "M 1" will be stored in loco.protocol

class electrip.widgets.TreeView(name)[source]¶

Bases: gi.overrides.Gtk.TreeView

A simplified TreeView, allowing to easily add columns and transport changes back to a datamodel.

name specifies the name of the TreeView, used for the ‘unsaved-changes’-messages.

Example:

class CustomTreeView(TreeView):
    def __init__(self):
        widgets.TreeView.__init__(self, "CustomTreeView")
        self.add_text_colum("Name of the column",
                            "A nice column",
                            GObject.TYPE_STRING)
        self.add_non_editable_text_colum("Sound file",
                                         "The sound to be played "
                                         "('*.wav' or '*.ogg')",
                                         GObject.TYPE_STRING)
        # self.add_more_stuff ...
        self.update_model()
        
        # we can connect to double-clicks as follows:
        # (assuming we created a handler 'choose_sound')
        self.connect("row-activated", self.choose_sound)
add_column(column_name, column_tooltip, cell_renderer, content_type)[source]¶

Adds a new column using cell_renderer.

add_combo_colum(column_name, column_tooltip, content_type, values)[source]¶

Adds a column with Gtk.ComboBox-widgets.

For column_name and column_tooltip see add_text_column(). content_type defines the type of the values to be stored in the combobox (e.g. str, float ...). values is a list of the values the user can choose from.

add_non_editable_text_colum(column_name, column_tooltip, content_type)[source]¶

Adds a column with non-editable text. For arguments, see add_text_column().

add_text_colum(column_name, column_tooltip, content_type)[source]¶

Adds a column with editable text. The column_name is displayed above the column and the column_tooltip appears when the mouse hovers over the colums header.

new_value(cellrenderer, path, new_value)[source]¶
save_changes(path, column_nr, new_value)[source]¶

This method is called whenever a value of a cell in the TreeView has changed. Child classes should make use of this.

path: a Gtk.TreePath to the respective cell. column_nr: number of the column where the change occured new_value: the new value of the cell

update_model()[source]¶

Overwrites the old liststore (if there is any) with the current column-setup. Must be called after all columns have been added.

class electrip.widgets.TreeViewActionBox(treeview, add_row_label, remove_row_label)[source]¶

Bases: gi.repository.Gtk.ButtonBox

A Gtk.ButtonBox providing Buttons for adding, removing and moving rows in a Gtk.TreeView.

treeview is the Gtk.TreeView-instance the TreeViewActionBox should operate on. add_row_label and remove_row_label specify the labels displayed on the buttons used for adding and removing rows.

add_row(button, treeview)[source]¶

Internal method.

add_row_at_start()[source]¶

Called when the user has asked the TreeViewActionBox to add a new row at the start-position of the TreeView. Must be implemented in a child class and return a list representing the data in the new row. E.g. if the TreeView consists of a name- and a description-column, the list could be ["some name", "the description"].

add_row_beneath(row_nr)[source]¶

Called when the user has asked the TreeViewActionBox to add a new row beneath row_nr. Must be implemented in a child class and return a list representing the data in the new row (see add_row_at_start()).

move_row(button, treeview, direction)[source]¶

Internal method.

move_row_down(row_nr)[source]¶

Called when the TreeViewActionBox has moved the row with row_nr one position downwards (row_nr + 1). Must be implemented in a child class to force it to update its datamodel.

move_row_up(row_nr)[source]¶

Called when the TreeViewActionBox has moved the row with row_nr one position upwards (row_nr - 1). Must be implemented in a child class to force it to update its datamodel.

remove_row(button, treeview)[source]¶

Internal method.

remove_row_at(row_nr)[source]¶

Called when the TreeViewActionBox has removed the row with row_nr. Must be implemented in a child class to force it to update its datamodel.

unsaved_changes()[source]¶

Called whenever changes were made to the data in the TreeView (reordering, deleting rows etc.). Allows child classes to get notified when these changes occur. Must not necessarily be implemented.
